transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Aurelia ML), Daniel Kwan (Aurelia SRE), Priya Nair (Aurelia Product), Alex Ortega (Aurelia DS)
Links mentioned: redwood-internal/quant-matrix-v2.xlsx, https://redwood.ai/pilot-pricing (shared), aurelia-shared/flagged-prompts.csv

Summary:
Quick status check on INT8/FP8 pilot. Reviewed quality deltas on three model families, confirmed one reproducible regression pattern for instruction-following prompts, discussed fallback policy and SLA targets, agreed on runbook for dedicated benchmark and next tuning steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, quick round robin, say who you are.
[00:05] Sofia Ramirez: hi this is Sofia, ML engineering, I'm on the quant experiments.
[00:07] Daniel Kwan: Daniel here, SRE, I'll be handling infra and tests.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Priya product, focusing on success metrics and rollout.
[00:13] Alex Ortega: Alex, DS, I did the eval script.
[00:15] Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood SE, running the tuning and kernels side.
[00:18] Maya Patel: and Maya AE, i'll coordinate next steps and pricing. ravi also on the call for deeper perf questions.
[00:25] Ravi Kapoor: yeah hi all.

[00:30] Maya Patel: quick agenda, 1) perf numbers since last week, 2) quality regressions and triage, 3) fallback / routing policy, 4) next steps. any additions?
[00:40] Sofia Ramirez: nope good.

[00:45] Liam Chen: ok i'll start with perf. we ran the week two suite on the same baseline config, models were: titan-7b-unfused (float32 baseline), then INT8 quantized, and FP8 mixed for the larger 13B family. results in the shared csv.
[01:05] Liam Chen: headline: INT8 gives ~2.8x throughput improvement on our infra with a median token latency improvement of 45% at 512 seq. FP8 gave 1.9x throughput with slightly better quality on some instruction prompts but higher variance on tail latency.
[01:25] Daniel Kwan: can you clarify the tail numbers? our SLA target is p99 < 250ms for 32 token responses, right?
[01:32] Liam Chen: right. for INT8 p99 under the synthetic steady run was around 210ms, fp8 p99 jumped to 320ms in a few runs due to kernel fallbacks when the KV cache warmed up.
[01:45] Priya Nair: fp8 320ms is concerning, that's over our acceptable p99. is that reproducible?
[01:50] Liam Chen: it was intermittent, so not consistently reproducible across 10 runs. we suspect kernel scheduling + memory spilling on the host side. we'll instrument traces to see whether it's a hot spot in the compile path.

[02:05] Alex Ortega: on the quality side, we ran 5 eval suites: hallucination, instruction-following, summarization, medical-QA, and triage ranking. INT8 had small drop in instruction-following F1 (~2.3%), fp8 had negligible drop (~0.6%) except one prompt family where FP8 hallucinated more for pipe-structured outputs.
[02:30] Sofia Ramirez: that's the prompt family I flagged last week, the one with enumerated outputs. we saw a consistent token misordering with INT8 in some seeds.
[02:40] Liam Chen: yes we isolated that to a transformer layer execution rounding behavior that affects beam scoring for enumerated outputs. we have a mitigation — switch to biased-softmax ordering for the affected outputs to stabilize beam scores — which we validated reduces the misorder by ~80% in a small ablation.
[02:58] Priya Nair: is that mitigation something we can enable at runtime per-route? we prefer not to change model weights for the pilot.
[03:05] Liam Chen: yes that's runtime config. Redwood's serving runtime supports per-route post-processing hooks; we can flip that flag for the specific route handling enumerations.

[03:20] Maya Patel: ok so mitigation path exists. now let's talk about the reproducible regression pattern you mentioned in the notes, Sofia.
[03:28] Sofia Ramirez: yeah, two prompt clusters: one with enumerated outputs (as Alex said) and one with medical QA templates where the model adds extraneous steps. that second cluster has lower recall under INT8 by about 4-5%.
[03:40] Alex Ortega: the medical QA cases are shorter-context, 40-80 tokens, and the error is mostly addition of irrelevant diagnostic steps. seems like calibration shifted.
[03:50] Liam Chen: that sounds like a softmax temperature/precision rounding artifact. we can try per-request temperature adjustment or an output filter that strips unlikely tokens — both are doable server-side.

[04:05] Daniel Kwan: quick infra question — if we enable per-route hooks and fallback to float32 for flagged prompts, how expensive is the routing decision? is this an extra network hop?
[04:15] Ravi Kapoor: it's actually an in-proxy decision, negligible added latency (~5-15ms) if done with regex/metadata, but if we do content-based routing with on-the-fly scoring it adds ~30-60ms. we should avoid heavy content scoring in the hot path.

[04:35] Priya Nair: what's the recommended fallback policy? always fallback to float32 for any flagged prompt, or do progressive degrade (FP8 -> INT8 -> float32)?
[04:45] Liam Chen: we recommend progressive: try FP8 (lower cost) if quality ok, else INT8 fallback, and as last resort float32. but given your strict p99 constraint, you might prefer FP8 only for non-latency-critical routes and INT8 for high-throughput stable routes, and float32 reserved for critical QA prompts.

[05:05] Sofia Ramirez: question: are the INT8 regressions fixed by the biased-softmax or do we still need fallback?
[05:12] Liam Chen: biased-softmax removes most ordering issues but does not recover the full recall loss on medical QA. for that we think a small dynamic temperature bump or route-level float32 fallback for that prompt cluster is safer.

[05:30] Maya Patel: let's talk about metrics for pilot success — Priya can you confirm product-level threshold?
[05:36] Priya Nair: we want max 2% drop on our top-5 business-critical prompt families measured by our current eval harness, and p99 <= 250ms for any route with SLA. cost savings target is 30% over float baseline for production.

[05:52] Alex Ortega: note our eval harness weights medical QA more heavily — so a 4% drop there will blow your weighted metric above 2%.

[06:00] Maya Patel: ok then we'll prioritize fixing the medical QA wobble. Liam, what's plan?
[06:05] Liam Chen: immediate plan: 1) instrument more traces to capture where fp8 kernel fallbacks happen 2) run a targeted tuning sweep for INT8 per-layer quant params focused on the top 3 layers implicated in beam scoring 3) produce a tuned INT8 variant that includes the biased-softmax postprocess.

[06:25] Sofia Ramirez: how long for that sweep?
[06:28] Liam Chen: quick sweep is 48 hours, deeper ablation could be 5 business days. we'll do the quick one and share v2 artifacts.

[06:35] Maya Patel: action item for Liam to share tuning matrix and a README.

[06:40] Daniel Kwan: on the dedicated benchmark you mentioned — do we need dedicated nodes for that?
[06:44] Ravi Kapoor: yes for an apples-to-apples p99 measurement we prefer dedicated pools so the jitter from multi-tenant doesn't pollute results. Redwood Dedicated trial can spin up a 3-node pool for the run.

[06:55] Priya Nair: cost implications?
[06:58] Maya Patel: I'll share pilot pricing; rough ballpark for a week-long dedicated micro-pool is in the shared spreadsheet. we can also do a scaled-down sim on hosted but less reliable for tail metrics.

[07:12] Alex Ortega: about regressions, I want to confirm labelling: which examples should be flagged to trigger float fallback? threshold?
[07:19] Liam Chen: we recommend a rule set: 1) prompts in medical QA family flagged by route metadata 2) if per-prompt calibration score drops below 0.6 (your scorer), then fallback, 3) if enumerated output has beam score divergence > 0.4 absolute delta then enable biased-softmax only.

[07:40] Sofia Ramirez: implementing the scorer is straightforward, we'll do that.

[07:45] Maya Patel: training data privacy and audit question — Aurelia wants logs scrubbed and KMS encryption, is that still supported in Dedicated pilot?
[07:52] Liam Chen: yes Dedicated supports customer KMS and audit logging. there is an onboarding checklist — we'll share the security playbook.

[08:02] Daniel Kwan: also need SOC2 attestation docs for procurement, priya asked for it earlier.
[08:07] Maya Patel: noted, will attach security packet in follow-up.

[08:12] (short pause)

[08:20] Alex Ortega: one oddity — in the FP8 runs we saw a high variance with certain batch sizes, specifically batches of 8 had better tail than batch of 4, which is counterintuitive. any idea?
[08:30] Ravi Kapoor: that often points to batching/kernel scheduling interplay; sometimes the larger batch triggers a different kernel path that's more optimized. we'll profile kernel selection heuristics.

[08:45] Sofia Ramirez: can we also try a small learning-free calibration step — like layernorm rescaling?
[08:50] Liam Chen: yes micro-calibration is cheap — we have a one-pass activation scaling routine that can reduce drift. that might help the medical QA recall.

[09:00] Priya Nair: who owns validating the micro-calibration? Aurelia or Redwood?
[09:04] Maya Patel: collaborative — Redwood will provide scripts and Aurelia runs them on the flagged set. then we compare metrics.

[09:10] Liam Chen: timeline: micro-calibration script -> 24 hours, quick INT8 sweep -> 48 hours, produce takeaways -> share by Friday EOD.

[09:22] Sofia Ramirez: ok we'll run flagged set against the scripts and post results.

[09:28] Maya Patel: any blockers from infra? Daniel?
[09:31] Daniel Kwan: just confirmation on peering; I'll check network posture and confirm by Monday. also need to validate the dedicated pool availability window.

[09:40] Priya Nair: decision on fallback policy — product leans to preserve accuracy for clinical routes and accept cost/latency hit. we'll accept float fallback for those routes.

[09:48] Liam Chen: ok we'll wire that in as a route-level policy; default progressive fallback remains otherwise.

[09:55] Alex Ortega: small ask — can Redwood include a column in the perf CSV that shows per-prompt quality delta and token-level latency? helps triage.
[09:59] Liam Chen: yes we'll add that.

[10:05] Maya Patel: recap: Liam to share tuning matrix and tuned variants, Redwood to share security packet and pricing, Aurelia to run flagged prompts and confirm peering, all to schedule dedicated benchmark tentatively next week.

[10:20] Priya Nair: sounds good.

[10:25] Maya Patel: last thing — do we want a short follow-up in 3 days or wait until we have tuning artifacts?
[10:30] Sofia Ramirez: let's do a 20-minute checkpoint in 3 days to align on tuning progress.

[10:35] Maya Patel: ok will schedule. thanks everyone.

[10:40] (end)
